event.label: Still listed in 1940, the last directory transcribed so far

body.p: Lansdowne Place is a lane off the south side of Queensberry Street. In 1860 the directory lists its entrance between Nos 10 and 12 Queensberry Street.

It is first listed in 1860. It is missing from the directories for 1862 to 1868, 1873, 1879 and 1880, and otherwise listed in every directory up to 1940, the last one transcribed so far. It never has more than about two dozen listings.

div.head: Along the street
div.p: From 1877 the directories give its corner with Queensberry Street as its only crossing.
The 1940 directory also lists a "Landsdowne Place" off Cardigan Street, with two houses. It may be a different lane.

list.item: The Melbourne City Council's electricity supply depot, listed from 1925 to 1940.

div.head: Records
div.p: Every directory and electoral-roll listing for Lansdowne Place can be browsed in search. Each directory year links to its own page from Sands & McDougall Directories.
